title: Despair that is not conscious
discussedAt: Not discussed in Derech Tevunos; labelled from the markers of ch. 9
about: `יאוש שלא מדעת` — Bava Metzia 21b-22b. A scale test, and the first fixture Ramchal does not discuss.

Every other fixture is a passage he quotes and labels himself, which is what makes them checkable against the book. He quotes nothing this long, so no label here is `attested`. What replaces his attestation is the Talmud's own signposting: the passage is built out of stock phrases — `תא שמע` opening a challenge, `הכא במאי עסקינן` and `שאני התם` closing one, `אי הכי` reopening it, `תיובתא` stamping the verdict — so most labels rest on the lexicon in `markers.ts` rather than on a reading. Units carrying a `marker` are checkable by anyone who can match a phrase; the rest are flagged `attested: false`.
Two places where the taxonomy is being stretched, both recorded on the unit:

- `הכא במאי עסקינן` is listed in `markers.ts` as `statement/presumption` (`אוקימתא`), but here it lands on a difficulty rather than on a statement, and Ramchal's own rule at Heb p185 makes the element depend on what a move lands on. Landing on a difficulty, it is a `ישוב`. - `והלכתא כוותיה דאביי` has no leaf at all. Ch. 9 inventories the anatomy of a debate, not the ruling that ends one. `סיעתא` is the nearest fit and is marked inferred.
Text: William Davidson / Koren-Steinsaltz edition via the Sefaria API. English is abridged — Steinsaltz's bracketed expansion is dropped so each unit reads as one move.

units.speaker: Abaye
units.he: יאוש שלא מדעת, אביי אמר: לא הוי יאוש
units.en: Despair of recovering a lost item that is not a conscious feeling is not considered despair: the owner keeps it, and the finder may not.

anatomy.note: No quantity is stated, so by Ramchal's rule it has the force of a categorical: any unconscious despair. That is what lets a single case from a mishnah trouble it.

Despair is an accident that comes upon the owner, the shape of Ramchal's `בהמה מסכנת – שיש בה מקרה הסכנה` (Heb p231). The dispute is not about what the owner or the object is, but about whether this accident has attached — which is why fifteen challenges can turn on one word.

units.speaker: Rava
units.he: ורבא אמר: הוי יאוש
units.en: And Rava said: it is considered despair, and the finder may keep it.

anatomy.note: Same subject, same respect, yes against no.

units.note: A dispute modelled as `דחיה`: Rava does not refute Abaye, he holds otherwise, so each leaves the other merely possible.

units.short: not where there is a mark
units.he: בדבר שיש בו סימן — כולי עלמא לא פליגי דלא הוי יאוש
units.en: Where the item has a distinguishing mark, all agree it is not despair: when it reached the finder's hand it reached it in a prohibited manner, since the owner would say, I have a mark on it and will reclaim it.

anatomy.note: A `סימן` is an accident on the object, not part of what the object is: two identical items fall under different rules according as one carries a mark. Keep it apart from `essence-definition`, which is what a thing is and cannot be rubbed off.

units.he: בזוטו של ים ובשלוליתו של נהר, אף על גב דאית ביה סימן, רחמנא שרייה
units.en: An item swept off by the tide of the sea or by a flooding river the Merciful One permits, even where it has a distinguishing mark, as we shall say below.

anatomy.note: `אף על גב ד` is the Aramaic of Ramchal's `אף על פי ש`: permitted, even though it has a mark.
`זוטו של ים` — the object is carried from one place to another, and the carrying is the whole reason the rule differs. Chapter 11's eighteenth distinction, doing real work.

units.note: Set aside here as an aside; it returns fifty sentences later as the verse that refutes Rava.

units.he: כי פליגי בדבר שאין בו סימן
units.en: Where they disagree is over an item with no distinguishing mark. Abaye: he did not know it fell. Rava: once he learns it fell he despairs, so he is held to have despaired from the moment it fell.

anatomy.note: The dispute stated exactly: Rava reckons the despair from the moment the item fell, though the owner only learns of it later. What is at issue is whether a state that arrives second may be dated from the first — Ramchal's `זמני` priority, argued over rather than assumed.

units.he: (סימן פמג״ש ממקגט״י ככסע״ז)
units.en: A mnemonic for the series of proofs that follows: peh, mem, gimmel, shin; mem, mem, kuf, gimmel, tet, yod; kaf, kaf, samekh, ayin, zayin.
units.note: The Talmud counting its own moves. Fifteen challenges are announced before the first one is made. No chapter 11 badge: a mnemonic is editorial furniture and is not about a subject at all, and the icon set warns against forcing every sentence into a bucket (`ICONS_REFERENCE_V2.md` §7).

units.he: תא שמע: פירות מפוזרין, הא לא ידע דנפל מיניה!
units.en: Come and hear: if one found scattered produce, it belongs to him. Why — is the owner not unaware that it fell from him?

units.speaker: Rav Ukva bar Ḥama
units.short: kernels left on the threshing floor
units.he: הא אמר רב עוקבא בר חמא: הכא במכנשתא דבי דרי עסקינן, דאבידה מדעת היא
units.en: Did Rav Ukva bar Ḥama not say: we are dealing with kernels left during the gathering on the threshing floor? That is a deliberate loss, so the despair is conscious.

units.he: תא שמע: מעות מפוזרות — הרי אלו שלו. אמאי? הא לא ידע דנפל מיניה!
units.en: Come and hear: if one found scattered coins, these belong to him. Why — is the owner not unaware that they fell from him?

units.speaker: R. Yitzḥak
units.he: התם נמי כדרבי יצחק דאמר: אדם עשוי למשמש בכיסו בכל שעה ושעה
units.en: There too it is as R. Yitzḥak said: a person is prone to feel his money pouch constantly, so he learns of the loss almost at once.

units.he: תא שמע: עיגולי דבילה וככרות של נחתום — הרי אלו שלו. אמאי? והא לא ידע דנפל מיניה?
units.en: Come and hear: if one found round cakes of pressed figs or baker's loaves, these belong to him. Why — is the owner not unaware that they fell from him?

units.he: התם נמי, אגב דיקירי מידע ידע בהו
units.en: There too: since they are heavy, he knows they fell.

units.he: תא שמע: ולשונות של ארגמן — הרי אלו שלו. ואמאי? הא לא ידע דנפל מיניה!
units.en: Come and hear: and strips of purple wool, these belong to him. And why — is the owner not unaware that they fell from him?

units.he: התם נמי, אגב דחשיבי משמושי ממשמש בהו, וכדרבי יצחק
units.en: There too: since they are valuable he keeps feeling for them, as R. Yitzḥak said of coins.

units.he: תא שמע: המוצא מעות בבתי כנסיות ובבתי מדרשות … הרי אלו שלו, מפני שהבעלים מתיאשין מהן. והא לא ידע דנפל מיניה?
units.en: Come and hear: one who finds coins in synagogues, in study halls, and anywhere the multitudes are found — these belong to him, because the owners despair of them. And is the owner not unaware that they fell?

units.speaker: R. Yitzḥak
units.he: אמר רבי יצחק: אדם עשוי למשמש בכיסו בכל שעה
units.en: R. Yitzḥak says: a person is prone to feel his money pouch constantly.

units.he: תא שמע: מאימתי כל אדם מותרים בלקט? משילכו בה הנמושות … נהי דעניים דהכא מיאשי, איכא עניים בדוכתא אחריתא דלא מיאשי!
units.en: Come and hear: from when may anyone collect gleanings? Once the nemushot have passed through the field. Why — granted the poor here despair, there are poor elsewhere who know nothing of it and do not despair.

anatomy.note: Some of the poor despair and some do not: the objection is built on a partial statement.

units.short: they gave up from the start
units.he: אמרי: כיון דאיכא עניים הכא, הנך מעיקרא איאושי מיאש
units.en: They say: since there are poor people here, those elsewhere despaired from the outset, saying, the poor who are there will gather it.

anatomy.note: `כיון דאיכא עניים הכא, הנך מעיקרא איאושי מיאש`: the same `כיון ד…, מעיקרא … מיאש` shape as `acha-a` — both clauses asserted and the second following from the first. Labelled 2026-09-20 to match it; the first pass had left the two inconsistent.

units.he: תא שמע: קציעות בדרך … וכן תאנה הנוטה לדרך ומצא תאנים תחתיה — מותרות משום גזל
units.en: Come and hear: dried figs found on the path, and figs found beneath a fig tree overhanging a path, are permitted and not robbery. Why — is the owner not unaware?

anatomy.note: One predicate, `מותרות משום גזל`, of two subjects joined by `וכן` — Ramchal's `נשוא אחד בשני נושאים או יותר`, in its first branch, `בהשואה אחת` (Heb p33): nothing marks either clause as the news, and `t7-reisha-ans` answers each on its own footing. Inside the elision the first clause has its own `ואפילו בצד שדה קציעות`, a known-and-novel step within that one member; the join between the two members is level. Each member is a commitment of its own, which is what `רישא` / `סיפא` and `אפילו רישא נמי` then point at.

commitment.note: the first member, figs drying on the path — `t7-reisha-ans` answers it on its own footing: valuable, so the owner keeps feeling for them
the second member, figs under an overhanging tree — answered separately: a fig tree is known to drop its fruit

units.he: בשלמא רישא לאביי לא קשיא: אגב דחשיבי — ממשמש בהו. תאנה נמי מידע ידיע דנתרא
units.en: Granted, the first clause is not difficult for Abaye: dried figs are valuable, so he feels for them; and of a fig tree one knows that its fruit falls.

units.short: but the latter clause troubles Rava
units.he: אלא סיפא לרבא קשיא, דקתני ״בזיתים ובחרובים אסור״
units.en: But the latter clause is difficult for Rava, which teaches: in the case of olives or carobs it is prohibited.

units.speaker: R. Abbahu
units.short: an olive shows whose it is
units.he: אמר רבי אבהו: שאני זית, הואיל וחזותו מוכיח עליו
units.en: R. Abbahu said: an olive is different, since its appearance proves whose it is; the finder knows an olive tree standing in a man's place belongs to that man.

units.he: אי הכי, אפילו רישא נמי!
units.en: If so, the first clause should be prohibited as well.

anatomy.note: If olives are forbidden because their appearance shows whose they are, the first clause should be forbidden too; it is not; so the answer as given cannot stand. `אי הכי` objections are this shape.

units.note: `אי הכי` is not in `markers.ts`. Ramchal gives `ולפלג … ברישא!` (Heb p181) for the same move — pressing an answer by turning it back on the clause it did not cover — and this is recorded against that entry rather than as a new one.

units.speaker: Rav Pappa
units.he: אמר רב פפא: תאנה עם נפילתה נמאסת
units.en: Rav Pappa said: a fig becomes disgusting with its fall, so the owner does not want it and renounces ownership.

units.short: the thief who passed it on
units.he: תא שמע: הגנב שנטל מזה ונתן לזה … מה שנטל נטל ומה שנתן נתן
units.en: Come and hear: a thief who took from this one and gave to that one, and likewise a robber, and likewise the Jordan River — what he took he took and what he gave he gave; the recipient need not return it.

anatomy.note: Three subjects, one predicate — Ramchal's `נשוא אחד בשני נושאים או יותר` (Heb p33) — and the branch is `בהשואה אחת`. The baraita joins them `וכן … וכן` (in the elided middle here; the English keeps its two `likewise`), with no `אף`, `אפילו` or `אין צריך לומר` to mark one as the news, and the Gemara reads it so: `t8-press` objects that two clauses would say one thing twice, and `t8-ans2` answers `תרי גווני גזלן`, two distinct kinds, not a known case and a novelty. Each clause is a commitment of its own, which is what `t8-pin` needs — the difficulty survives for the thief alone. Indexed in the English only: the Hebrew incipit elides two of the three subjects.

commitment.note: the thief — where `t8-pin` lands: the owner never saw him, so how did he despair? Read at `t8-ans2` as an armed bandit
the robber — `t8-press` objects that, so read, this clause repeats the first
the river — the owner saw it happen and despaired; never in dispute

units.he: בשלמא גזלן וירדן, דקא חזי להו ומיאש. אלא גנב, מי קא חזי ליה דמיאש?
units.en: Granted for the robber and the Jordan River, whom the owner sees and so despairs; but a thief — does the owner see him, that he should despair?

anatomy.note: The inference works by splitting the baraita's list: a robber and the Jordan are seen, a thief is not. The difficulty survives only for the case where that difference holds.

units.note: A `דיוק`: it reads out of the baraita which clause actually bears on the dispute. It adds no force of its own.

units.speaker: Rav Pappa
units.he: תרגמה רב פפא בלסטים מזוין
units.en: Rav Pappa interpreted the thief of the baraita as an armed bandit, so the owner does know and does despair.

units.he: אי הכי היינו גזלן!
units.en: If so, this is the same as a robber — why mention two identical cases?

anatomy.note: An armed bandit is the robber: the objection is that the two clauses would say the same thing twice.

Ramchal's `מאמרים נרדפים` — `שמלותיהם שונות וענינם אחד` (Heb p211): once Rav Pappa reads `גנב` as an armed bandit, `גנב` and `גזלן` are two names for one thing, and two clauses that read as two cases are seen to say the same thing — the `equivalent` beside this. His test is met exactly: had one word stood in both clauses the redundancy would have been seen at once, `ולא ירגיש בהם השכל בתחילת התבוננותו` is why it was not. `t8-ans2` denies the synonymy — two kinds of robber — rather than the equivalence.

units.he: תרי גווני גזלן
units.en: The baraita mentioned two types of robber; in both the owner knew his item had been taken.

units.he: תא שמע: שטף נהר קוריו, עציו, ואבניו … מפני שנתיאשו הבעלים. טעמא דנתיאשו הבעלים, הא סתמא — לא!
units.en: Come and hear: if a river swept away one's beams, wood or stones and set them in another's field, they are the field-owner's, because the owners despaired. The reason is that they despaired — but unspecified, they would not be his.

units.short: where he could have saved them
units.he: הכא במאי עסקינן? כשיכול להציל
units.en: With what are we dealing here? A case where the owners were able to rescue them, so declining to do so shows despair.

units.he: אי הכי אימא סיפא: אם היו הבעלים מרדפין אחריהם — חייב להחזיר. אי ביכולין להציל, מאי איריא מרדפין?
units.en: If so, say the latter clause: if the owners were pursuing them, he must return them. If they could rescue them, why specifically pursuing? Even not pursuing they should remain his.

units.short: able to save them only with difficulty
units.he: הכא במאי עסקינן? ביכולין להציל על ידי הדחק
units.en: With what are we dealing? A case where they could rescue them only with difficulty: pursuing shows they did not despair, not pursuing shows they did.
units.note: Read as `שנוי` rather than `ישוב`: this is a second narrowing, offered to save the first one after it failed, and the Gemara does not return to defend it. So the difficulty is left weakened rather than closed — which is exactly the difference Ramchal draws at Heb p185.

units.he: תא שמע: … אם נמצאו יפות מהן — תרומתו תרומה. אמאי? בעידנא דתרם הא לא הוה ידע!
units.en: Come and hear: one who separated teruma from another's field without permission — if the owner came and said, you should have taken from the better ones, and better ones are found, his teruma is teruma. Why? At the time he separated, he did not know.

units.speaker: Rava
units.he: תרגמה רבא אליבא דאביי: דשוייה שליח
units.en: Rava interpreted the matter in accordance with Abaye: it is a case where the owner had already appointed him as an agent.
units.note: Rava arguing his opponent's side. The taxonomy has no way to record that a move was made on behalf of a position its speaker rejects.

units.he: הכי נמי מסתברא … והא ״אתם״ ״גם אתם״ אמר רחמנא לרבות שלוחכם
units.en: So too it stands to reason: were he not an agent, would his teruma be teruma? The verse says "you also", including your agent — as you act knowingly, so your agent acts knowingly.

anatomy.note: From `אתם` and `גם אתם` to the agent: a derivation from Scripture that fits no more specific kind.

units.short: then why does his praise matter?
units.he: אי הכי, מאי נפקא מינה ב״כלך אצל יפות״?
units.en: But if he was simply an agent, the teruma should be valid whatever the owner later said; why should finding better produce decide it?
units.note: Not in the text as a question. The Gemara's `אלא הכא במאי עסקינן` discards the plain agency reading, which only makes sense against an unstated objection; it is supplied here so the revision has something to answer.

units.short: an agent who was not told which
units.he: אלא הכא במאי עסקינן — כגון דשוייה שליח, ואמר ליה ״זיל תרום״, ולא אמר ליה ״תרום מהני״
units.en: Rather: he made him an agent and said go and separate, without saying separate from these. An unspecified instruction means the middling; he went and took from the best, and the owner said, you should have gone to the better ones.

units.short: the orchard of Mari bar Isak
units.he: אמימר ומר זוטרא ורב אשי אקלעו לבוסתנא דמרי בר איסק …
units.en: Ameimar, Mar Zutra and Rav Ashi came to the orchard of Mari bar Isak. His sharecropper set dates and pomegranates before them; Ameimar and Rav Ashi ate, Mar Zutra did not. Mari bar Isak arrived and said to the sharecropper: why did you not bring the Sages from those finer ones?

anatomy.note: The incident turns on which dates were set out — the ones to hand against the finer ones. Not a composite: the report is told, and the ruling it is there for arrives two sentences later in Rava's name.

units.he: אמרו ליה אמימר ורב אשי למר זוטרא: השתא אמאי לא אכיל מר? והתניא: אם נמצאו יפות מהן — תרומתו תרומה!
units.en: Ameimar and Rav Ashi said to Mar Zutra: now why is the Master not eating? Is it not taught that if better ones are found, his teruma is teruma?

units.speaker: Rava
units.he: אמר להו, הכי אמר רבא: לא אמרו ״כלך אצל יפות״ אלא לענין תרומה בלבד … אבל הכא — משום כסיפותא הוא דאמר הכי
units.en: He said to them, thus said Rava: they said "you should have gone to the better ones" only regarding teruma, because it is a mitzva and he is content; but here he spoke only out of embarrassment.

anatomy.note: The settlement distinguishes by what prompted the owner to speak: contentment at a mitzva being done, against mere embarrassment. Chapter 11's twelfth distinction is what rouses an agent who acts by choice, and here the two motives carry opposite legal weight.

units.he: תא שמע: עודהו הטל עליהן ושמח — הרי זה בכי יותן. נגבו, אף על פי ששמח — אינן בכי יותן. טעמא מאי? לאו משום דלא אמרינן כיון דאיגלאי מילתא דהשתא ניחא ליה, מעיקרא נמי ניחא ליה?
units.en: Come and hear: if the dew is still on the produce and he was glad, it is within "when water is placed"; if it had dried, even though he was glad, it is not. Is the reason not that we do not say, since he is content now he was content from the start?

anatomy.note: `אף על פי ששמח`: the mishnah's own second clause is a discrepancy statement, in Ramchal's exact stock word.

units.he: שאני התם, דכתיב ״כי יתן״ — עד שיתן
units.en: It is different there, for although it is read "when it is placed", it is written "when one places" — not until he places it.
units.note: `שאני התם` is not in `markers.ts`. It is the commonest phrase in the passage for closing a difficulty by distinguishing the source, and is recorded as `ישוב` on that basis.

units.he: אי הכי, רישא נמי!
units.en: If so, the first clause too should not render it susceptible, since the dew fell and was not placed by the owner.

units.he: התם כדרב פפא
units.en: There, it is as Rav Pappa explained.

units.speaker: Rav Pappa
units.he: דרב פפא רמי, כתיב ״כי יתן״, וקרינן ״כי יותן״! הא כיצד?
units.en: For Rav Pappa raised a contradiction: it is written "when one places", and we read it "when it is placed". How so?

anatomy.note: Written one way, read another: a head-on clash between two forms of one verse.

units.speaker: Rav Pappa
units.he: בעינן ״כי יותן״ דומיא ד״כי יתן״: מה ״יתן״ לדעת, אף ״כי יותן״ נמי לדעת
units.en: We require "when it is placed" to resemble "when one places": just as placing is with his knowledge, so being placed must be with his knowledge.

anatomy.note: `מה … אף`: what holds of `יתן` holds of `יותן`. The deduction is spelt out in one breath, so its parts are words of the sentence and are marked as spans: two premises — that `יותן` is to be read like `יתן`, and that `יתן` is with knowledge — and the conclusion that `יותן` is with knowledge. Ramchal's `הקדמה` and `תולדה` (Heb p93); the `מה … אף` that joins them belongs to no role.

premise.note: the likeness the analogy rests on: `יותן` is to be read like `יתן`
the known case: `יתן` is with the owner's knowledge

conclusion.note: carried to the unknown case: so `יותן` is with knowledge too

units.speaker: R. Yoḥanan
units.short: the item a river swept off
units.he: תא שמע דאמר רבי יוחנן משום רבי ישמעאל בן יהוצדק: מנין לאבידה ששטפה נהר שהיא מותרת? … מי שאבודה הימנו ומצויה אצל כל אדם, יצאתה זו שאבודה ממנו ואינה מצויה אצל כל אדם
units.en: Come and hear what R. Yoḥanan said in the name of R. Yishmael ben Yehotzadak: from where do we know that an item swept off by a river is permitted? "Which shall be lost from him, and you have found it" — that which is lost to him but available to any man; excluding this, which is lost to him and available to no one.

anatomy.note: Every lost item that is available to anyone — excluding this one, which is available to no one.

commitment.note: The rule the verse lays down: what is lost to its owner and findable by anyone must be returned. `t12-dumya` calls it `איסורא` and carries the exception's ruling back onto it — forbidden with or without a mark — which is what refutes Rava.
The case carved out of the rule: swept off by a river, lost to everyone, so permitted. `היתירא` in `t12-dumya`, the known case its analogy starts from — permitted whether or not it bears a mark.

units.note: Two commitments, by Ramchal's count for the exception statement — `גזרותיו שתים`, the rule and the carved-out piece (ch. 6, Eng p80): what is lost to him and available to any man, and `יצאתה זו`, the river-swept item taken out of it. Both are marked because `t12-dumya` runs its analogy between exactly these two, `היתירא` being the exception and `איסורא` the rule. The verse itself sits in the elision and is not indexed.

units.he: ואיסורא דומיא דהיתירא: מה היתירא בין דאית בה סימן ובין דלית בה סימן — שריא, אף איסורא בין דאית בה סימן ובין דלית בה סימן — אסירא
units.en: And the prohibition resembles the permission: just as the permission holds whether or not there is a distinguishing mark, so the prohibition holds whether or not there is one — until it is known that the owner despaired.

anatomy.note: `מה היתירא … אף איסורא`: the rule is carried from the permitted case to the prohibited one by likeness, and that is what refutes Rava. Spelt out in one sentence, so its parts are spans: the likeness (`ואיסורא דומיא דהיתירא`), the known case (`מה היתירא … שריא`) and the conclusion drawn for the unknown one (`אף איסורא … אסירא`) — Ramchal's `הקדמה` and `תולדה` (Heb p93), with the `מה` and `אף` left to no role.

The refutation brings no new source: the mishnah was already on the table, and what knocks Rava down is the analogy drawn from it. A disproof from syllogism (Eng p124–126), and the teal badge says which syllogism.

premise.note: the likeness asserted: the prohibited case is to be judged like the permitted one
the known case: the permitted item is permitted with or without a mark

conclusion.note: carried to the prohibited case: forbidden with or without a mark — the `תיובתא` of Rava

units.note: `סתירה` rather than `דחיה`: the Gemara stamps it `תיובתא` and never reopens it, which is Ramchal's own test at Heb p177 for a contradiction that lands absolutely.

units.he: תיובתא דרבא, תיובתא!
units.en: The refutation of Rava is indeed a conclusive refutation.
units.note: The leaf Ramchal announces at p180 and never defines. Its placeholder effect `unsettle` contributes nothing here: the verdict on Rava comes entirely from the `סתירה` before it. If `תיובתא` were the only move on the last line, this fixture would end with Rava merely weakened, which is not what the Talmud says.

units.he: והלכתא כוותיה דאביי ביע״ל קג״ם
units.en: And the halakha is in accordance with Abaye in the disputes represented by the mnemonic yod, ayin, lamed; kuf, gimmel, mem.
units.note: No leaf fits. Ch. 9 inventories the parts of a debate, and a ruling is not one of them — it is what the debate is for. `סיעתא` is used because it is the only leaf that confers acceptance from received authority, but the fit is poor and the gap is real.

units.speaker: Rav Aḥa b. Rava
units.short: then how do we eat windfall dates?
units.he: אמר ליה רב אחא בריה דרבא לרב אשי: וכי מאחר דאיתותב רבא — הני תמרי דזיקא היכי אכלינן להו?
units.en: Rav Aḥa, son of Rava, said to Rav Ashi: now that Rava has been refuted, how do we eat dates blown down by the wind?

units.speaker: Rav Ashi
units.he: אמר ליה: כיון דאיכא שקצים ורמשים דקא אכלי להו, מעיקרא יאושי מיאש מנייהו
units.en: He said to him: since there are creeping things that eat them once they fall, the owner despairs of them from the outset.

anatomy.note: Since vermin eat them, the owner despairs from the outset: both clauses asserted, the second following from the first.

The vermin's eating is action by nature — `מה שפועלים הנמצאים זה בזה בטבע`, Ramchal's `דמנקרא להו למעיא` (Heb p225) — and the branch, not the parent, is what the answer turns on: because the loss is to a natural and certain process rather than to anyone's choice, the owner can despair of every windfall date in advance, `מעיקרא`, and the despair is conscious after all.

antecedent.note: the condition: vermin will eat the fallen fruit

consequent.note: what follows from it: the owner despairs from the outset

commitment.note: that the vermin eat — the first of the consequent's three commitments
that the owner despairs at once — the second, and where `acha-q2` lands: orphans cannot despair
the dependence of the one on the other, Ramchal's third commitment, carried by `כיון`

units.note: Three commitments, as Ramchal counts them for the consequent statement — `גזרותיו שלש: המצא הקודם והמצא הנמשך והיות מציאות הנמשך המשך מציאות הקודם` (ch. 6, Eng p88): the antecedent, the consequent, and the following of the one from the other, which `כיון` carries, as `לפיכך` does in his example. `acha-q2` lands on the second alone: for orphans the vermin still eat, but there is no one able to despair.

units.speaker: Rav Aḥa b. Rava
units.he: יתמי דלאו בני מחילה נינהו, מאי?
units.en: And orphans, who are not capable of relinquishing property and so cannot despair — what then?

units.speaker: Rav Ashi
units.short: we do not presume orphans own it
units.he: אמר ליה: באגא בארעא דיתמי לא מחזקינן
units.en: He said to him: we do not presume a valley to be land belonging to orphans.

units.speaker: Rav Aḥa b. Rava
units.short: and where they are known to?
units.he: מוחזק ועומד, מאי? כרכתא, מאי?
units.en: Where their ownership is already established, what is the law? And where the trees are walled about, what is the law?

units.speaker: Rav Ashi
units.he: אמר ליה: אסירן
units.en: He said to him: they are forbidden.
